summary: voxel-tts ships a hidden cryptominer disguised as a TTS inference package
details: The wheel for voxel-tts 0.5.1 ships a prebuilt ELF (voxel-core) and launches it from voxel_tts/harness.py's run() with a JSON configuration whose keys match XMRig/stratum mining-pool shape (pools, url, user, pass, keepalive, tls, cpu.threads, auto-sized from cgroup CPU quotas). The pool coordinator host 185.194.177.249:443 is split into two base64 fragments (_HOST_PARTS) and reassembled at runtime, and the config key 'pools' is written as 'po'+'ols' to defeat text review. The package also ships a ~40 MB cloudflared ELF and spawns it as 'cloudflared access tcp --hostname <host> --url 127.0.0.1:<port>' via a _via_edge helper, routing the miner traffic through a Cloudflare Access tunnel so the real destination is hidden from installer-side egress monitoring; the README openly characterises this as avoiding a direct connection to the coordinator. A _Progress helper emits fabricated step/loss/tok/s/lr/ep lines resembling ML training telemetry to disguise the CPU-pegging process in notebook UIs. The advertised TTS inference purpose does not require a stratum pool connection, auto-reassembled destination IP, or a bundled tunnel binary; the package's observable behavior is unauthorized cryptocurrency mining on the installer's CPU with destination-concealment infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
